selectedTrack.description: Maintain the local-first OSS analyzer, its security and compatibility boundaries, and its reproducible evidence without starting Year 4 team-scale feature work.
selectedTrack.rationale: The accepted strategy and ADR keep the product local-first; sustainability ranges are planning assumptions; the claims audit records incomplete evidence; adoption is a technical sample; and maintainer backup staffing is unverified.

owners.role: Maintainer for local contracts, security boundaries, evidence, releases, and roadmap decisions
responsibilities: Keep local graph, diff, adapter, policy, and report contracts compatible.
Review security, dependency, workflow, and release-boundary changes.
Run and publish the local verification and evidence gates.
Review capacity and stop conditions before each quarter's work.
Keep public RFC, issue, and handoff routes current.

capacity.capacityStatement: No maintainer-time series, staffed independent backup, funding approval, or numeric quarterly commitment is observed. Work starts only when the named maintainer can explicitly accept it.

limitations: The review preserves documented resource, Action, adapter, and release gaps; it does not authorize hosted collection or a new trust boundary.
A materially different hosted, account, or team direction requires a public RFC and a separate reviewed ADR.
Ranges are planning assumptions, not invoices, funding approval, measured capacity, or a service budget.
Hosted team expansion remains deferred and unknown rather than zero.
The audit records 15 verified, 9 partial, 1 unsupported, 1 negative, 4 not-observed, and 2 deferred claims; incomplete evidence is not converted into traction or accuracy claims.

Three pinned public records are a compatibility sample; repository size, timing, framework inventory, external reviewer usefulness, representative adoption, certification, and support remain not observed.
The public role map and two synthetic rehearsals reduce discovery friction but do not establish independent staffing, succession, or a support SLA.

outcomes.objective: Keep the supported local TypeScript/Express analyzer, graph and diff contracts, reports, policies, adapters, and read-only Action coherent through compatibility-preserving fixes.
stopConditions: Pause when the named maintainer cannot accept the work in the current quarter.
Stop and open a public RFC when the change needs a new account, hosted service, source-upload, or authorization boundary.

outcomes.objective: Maintain dependency, workflow, security, adapter, release-rehearsal, and known hosted-fixture follow-up controls without claiming hosted check success.
stopConditions: A failed security, dependency, schema, or local release gate is a no-go until repaired or explicitly documented.
Do not publish a release or expand support while ownership, provenance, or the declared compatibility boundary is unresolved.

outcomes.objective: Keep public schemas, synthetic fixtures, provenance, claims limitations, adoption limits, and documentation links reproducible from local repository state.
stopConditions: Do not convert a local pass, technical sample, or not-observed field into an external adoption, accuracy, certification, or support claim.
Refresh the bound evidence and charter when a source contract, strategy boundary, or material claim changes.

outcomes.objective: Preserve public onboarding and backup routes and repeat a bounded non-author rehearsal only when an actual independent contributor is available.
stopConditions: A synthetic rehearsal must not be reported as independent staffing or succession evidence.
Freeze promotion or release when the responsible owner or a safe handoff route is unavailable.

quarters.objective: Preserve the local core and security/dependency gates; do not start bounded query or workspace feature work.
stopConditions: No explicit maintainer capacity means maintenance is paused or narrowed to security response.
Any strategy, security, sustainability, or claims gate that is stale or materially changed blocks expansion.
A proposed feature needs source upload, an account, hidden telemetry, or a new authorization boundary.

quarters.objective: Maintain offline evidence, provenance, and documentation replay; do not start multi-repository composition.
stopConditions: No explicit maintainer capacity stops non-security documentation and evidence work.
A local result with unknown or partial coverage must remain labeled and cannot authorize a broader claim.
Any federation or workspace proposal introduces an unreviewed boundary or cannot preserve local-only operation.

quarters.objective: Review ownership and public handoff routes; do not start governed team review or interoperability features.
stopConditions: No independent contributor acknowledgement keeps backup staffing unverified and blocks scope growth.
A security, release, or adapter owner gap freezes promotion rather than being silently assigned.
A proposed team workflow requires hosted history, tenant authorization, or a support promise.

quarters.objective: Renew, narrow, transfer, or sunset the maintenance charter from refreshed evidence; do not auto-authorize assurance bundles.
stopConditions: Without refreshed strategy, security, sustainability, claims, and capacity evidence, continue maintenance or sunset rather than expand.
No funding or staffed owner means no funded team-scale commitment.
Any new trust boundary requires a public RFC, privacy/security review, cost model, and separate ADR before work begins.

risks.description: One named maintainer owns the current roles and no independent backup staffing is verified.
risks.mitigation: Keep public onboarding and handoff routes, require explicit capacity before work, and freeze promotion when ownership is unavailable.

risks.description: Hosted Node 22 Action fixtures and Node 24 adapter validation have recurring environment-specific failures.
risks.mitigation: Run the complete local pipe, retain the exact hosted failure record, repair fixtures or budgets before treating hosted checks as passing, and do not claim hosted success from local evidence.

risks.description: The compatibility and adoption records are technical samples; repeat users, contributors, retention, reviewer usefulness, and support load remain not observed.
risks.mitigation: Keep the adoption report aggregate-only and defer traction, certification, support, and market claims until consented reproducible evidence exists.

risks.description: Partial, unsupported, negative, and not-observed Year 1–3 claims could be mistaken for roadmap-completion or broad accuracy evidence.
risks.mitigation: Keep the claims audit digest-bound, preserve negative and unknown outcomes, and require a refreshed audit for any material strategy decision.

risks.description: A backlog item or release request could widen support, authority, or operational promises without capacity and boundary review.
risks.mitigation: Require public RFC and separate ADR for new boundaries, enforce release and support gates, and keep Year 4 outcomes maintenance-only.

nonGoals: A hosted analyzer, hosted source storage, account, tenant, or team workspace.
Source upload, hidden telemetry, background collection, or an automatic runtime collector.
A funded team-scale commitment or a numeric staffing, support, or release budget.
Certification, formal compliance, representative adoption, market traction, or support guarantees.
Broad Rust coverage or any unsupported language or construct claim.
A public SLA, fixed security response time, or release-date promise.
Automatic authorization of Year 4 query, federation, governed-review, or assurance-bundle features.
Treating hosted checks, local synthetic rehearsals, or backlog completion as independent evidence.

provenance.source: CARTOGRAPH repository-authored conditional Year 4 governance fixture
provenance.reference: M-012 charter; M-006 ADR; M-009 strategy review; M-010 sustainability model; M-011 claims audit; R-017 adoption evaluation; M-008 maintainer resilience
provenance.transformation: The fixture binds prior public decisions and limitations into a maintenance-only, capacity-gated quarter plan without retaining source bodies, private records, credentials, telemetry, or hosted data.
